Thanks for the report and the screenshot — helpful. I pulled the SAML trace and what we’re seeing is that the RelayState URL appended to the SAML response contains a long base64 token that is being truncated by our email sanitization/redirect step. When the vendor clicks Accept, the browser is redirected back to our SSO endpoint with an incomplete RelayState, which makes the IdP treat the assertion as malformed.

What I’ve done so far:
- Captured a full SAML response from your session (attached: saml-trace-20260923.txt).
- Pushed a hotfix to the cookie/redirect sanitizer that preserves RelayState up to 4096 chars (PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/runtime/pull/4567). The hotfix is in staging now and will go to production in ~30 minutes after smoke tests.
- As a stopgap, please try accepting the invite from an incognito window and make sure there are no email client link rewrites (some corporate mail gateways rewrite long querystrings). If that fails, open the raw invite link and paste it directly into the browser address bar instead of clicking the redirected button.

Asha — can you try the incognito flow now? If you run into the same error, send me the timestamp (your local time) and I’ll pull the live trace.

Attachments: saml-trace-20260923.txt (debug trace, redacted)
